Only needed to find and match the old video's material, or while the project still cuts shots out of it (`derive: {path: reference/...}`); a new video has none. devignette.description:

devignette.markdownDescription:

fit.description:
Make the whole picture fit inside `size`, centred, and fill the rest: `blur` (the default) with a blurred copy of the picture enlarged to cover it, `black` with black. Fits a portrait photo into a landscape frame without cropping it. With `blur`, `lighten: 0.35` (0-1) brightens the blurred copy - every channel times 1 + 5 x `lighten`, so its colours stay (a dark brown turns light brown, not grey) - for a dark picture (a cave, a night shot) whose blurred surround would otherwise look like plain black. As a **card** on its blurred copy (`blur` only): `margin: 60` keeps at least that many px of the copy all round the picture, `radius: 40` rounds its corners, `edge: 8` softens its edge over that many px, `shadow: 0.45` (0-1) lays a soft shadow of its shape under it, `dim: 0.2` (0-1) darkens the copy so the card stands out - e.g. `{size: [1920, 1080], background: blur, margin: 60, radius: 40, edge: 8, shadow: 0.45, dim: 0.2}`; any picture shape, a portrait one as a tall card. `margin`, `radius` and `edge` are whole pixels, `margin` less than half the smaller side of `size`; `shadow` and `dim` go from 0 up to (not including) 1; `dim` and `lighten` don't go together. On a video, the card's shape and shadow are worked out once, on its first frame.

Example: `{size: [1440, 960], background: blur}`
fit.markdownDescription:
Make the whole picture fit inside `size`, centred, and fill the rest: `blur` (the default) with a blurred copy of the picture enlarged to cover it, `black` with black. Fits a portrait photo into a landscape frame without cropping it. With `blur`, `lighten: 0.35` (0-1) brightens the blurred copy - every channel times 1 + 5 x `lighten`, so its colours stay (a dark brown turns light brown, not grey) - for a dark picture (a cave, a night shot) whose blurred surround would otherwise look like plain black. As a **card** on its blurred copy (`blur` only): `margin: 60` keeps at least that many px of the copy all round the picture, `radius: 40` rounds its corners, `edge: 8` softens its edge over that many px, `shadow: 0.45` (0-1) lays a soft shadow of its shape under it, `dim: 0.2` (0-1) darkens the copy so the card stands out - e.g. `{size: [1920, 1080], background: blur, margin: 60, radius: 40, edge: 8, shadow: 0.45, dim: 0.2}`; any picture shape, a portrait one as a tall card. `margin`, `radius` and `edge` are whole pixels, `margin` less than half the smaller side of `size`; `shadow` and `dim` go from 0 up to (not including) 1; `dim` and `lighten` don't go together. On a video, the card's shape and shadow are worked out once, on its first frame.

Example: `{size: [1440, 960], background: blur}`

feather.description:

feather.markdownDescription:

openshot.description:
libopenshot's effects, last of all, in order: video ones (`Wave`, `AnalogTape`, `LensFlare`, `SphericalProjection`, `Pixelate`, `ColorShift`, `Shift`, `Bars`...) and audio ones (`Echo`, `Robotization`, `Whisperization`, `Distortion`...). Each a map with its `effect` and any of its properties: a number, a map of seconds to numbers (keyframes), a colour (`[r, g, b]` or `"#rrggbb"`), `true`/`false` or text - checked against libopenshot's own catalog. `Caption` (draws nothing outside OpenShot's editor: use a `type: title` clip) and `Mask` (needs a mask picture it can't be given) are refused. Needs libopenshot's Python bindings (`python3-openshot`, which `openshot-qt` brings): run with the system's Python (`VIDEO_AS_CODE_OPENSHOT_PYTHON` for another). Not with `upscale`.

Example: `[{effect: Wave, amplitude: 0.6}]`
openshot.markdownDescription:
libopenshot's effects, last of all, in order: video ones (`Wave`, `AnalogTape`, `LensFlare`, `SphericalProjection`, `Pixelate`, `ColorShift`, `Shift`, `Bars`...) and audio ones (`Echo`, `Robotization`, `Whisperization`, `Distortion`...). Each a map with its `effect` and any of its properties: a number, a map of seconds to numbers (keyframes), a colour (`[r, g, b]` or `"#rrggbb"`), `true`/`false` or text - checked against libopenshot's own catalog. `Caption` (draws nothing outside OpenShot's editor: use a `type: title` clip) and `Mask` (needs a mask picture it can't be given) are refused. Needs libopenshot's Python bindings (`python3-openshot`, which `openshot-qt` brings): run with the system's Python (`VIDEO_AS_CODE_OPENSHOT_PYTHON` for another). Not with `upscale`.

Example: `[{effect: Wave, amplitude: 0.6}]`

source.description:

When several album items share that name, `source: {name: IMG-20150308-WA0003.jpg, taken: "2015-03-08 15:23:51"}` - the name plus its capture `taken` time (local, to the second) - says which one; if even the time ties, `size: [w, h]` (in pixels) too; if even that ties, `id:` - the album item's id, the `media_id` in `sources.lock.yaml` (see README's *`video-as-code fetch`*).

Example: `{id: slide, source: PXL_20250830_085416309.mp4}`

color_grade.description: Three-way colour grading: any of `lift` (shadows), `gamma` (midtones), `gain` (highlights), each `[r, g, b]`. Neutral is lift `[0,0,0]`, gamma and gain `[1,1,1]`; e.g. `{gamma: [1.2, 1.2, 1.2]}` brightens the midtones.
color_grade.markdownDescription: Three-way colour grading: any of `lift` (shadows), `gamma` (midtones), `gain` (highlights), each `[r, g, b]`. Neutral is lift `[0,0,0]`, gamma and gain `[1,1,1]`; e.g. `{gamma: [1.2, 1.2, 1.2]}` brightens the midtones.

color_grade_keyframes.description: A second grade on top of `color_grade`, animated: `[{at: 0, lift: [0, 0, 0]}, {at: 1.5, lift: [0.2, 0.18, 0.06]}]`, `at` in seconds into the clip (the first `0`, each later than the one before), every keyframe with the same groups; eased linearly from one to the next and held after the last. For a swell of light that rises and falls across clips, give each clip its stretch of it.
color_grade_keyframes.markdownDescription: A second grade on top of `color_grade`, animated: `[{at: 0, lift: [0, 0, 0]}, {at: 1.5, lift: [0.2, 0.18, 0.06]}]`, `at` in seconds into the clip (the first `0`, each later than the one before), every keyframe with the same groups; eased linearly from one to the next and held after the last. For a swell of light that rises and falls across clips, give each clip its stretch of it.

old_film.description: `true` turns on each "old film" filter (flicker and uneven developing, dust, scratches, grain).
old_film.markdownDescription: `true` turns on each "old film" filter (flicker and uneven developing, dust, scratches, grain).

film_dust.description:
`true` turns on each "old film" filter (flicker and uneven developing, dust, scratches, grain).

As a map: Instead of `true`: `style: svg` (the default) draws MLT's dust pictures, `size` percent of the clip's width across (default `2`); `dots` draws small round specks, darker and lighter, at most `size` pixels in radius (default `4`), like the dust on an old print. `count`: at most that many per frame (default `10`). One style per project: `dots` makes `render` run melt on a copy of its data folder without the dust pictures (opened in kdenlive, the project shows them). `pictures` (with `svg`): the pictures to pick from instead of MLT's five - theirs by name (`dust1`, `dust2` blots, the latter drawn white; `dust3`-`dust5` hairs) or `.svg` files of the project, a repeated one coming up more often; e.g. `[dust3, dust4, dust5, assets/speck.svg]`, the speck drawn small inside a larger transparent picture. One set per project, also by swapping the data folder. `hold`: the same specks for that many frames running (default `1`, new ones every frame).

Default: `{style: dots, size: 4, count: 10}`

One style per project: `dots` makes `render` run melt on a copy of its data folder without the dust pictures (opened in kdenlive, the project shows them). `pictures` (with `svg`): the pictures to pick from instead of MLT's five - theirs by name (`dust1`, `dust2` blots, the latter drawn white; `dust3`-`dust5` hairs) or `.svg` files of the project, a repeated one coming up more often; e.g. `[dust3, dust4, dust5, assets/speck.svg]`, the speck drawn small inside a larger transparent picture. One set per project, also by swapping the data folder. `hold`: the same specks for that many frames running (default `1`, new ones every frame).

Default: `{style: dots, size: 4, count: 10}`

film_scratches.description: `true` turns on each "old film" filter (flicker and uneven developing, dust, scratches, grain).
film_scratches.markdownDescription: `true` turns on each "old film" filter (flicker and uneven developing, dust, scratches, grain).

film_grain.description:
`true` turns on each "old film" filter (flicker and uneven developing, dust, scratches, grain).

As a map: Instead of `true`: grain that changes every frame, `noise` its strength (default `40`), with `contrast` and `brightness` in percent, `100` (the default) meaning unchanged. `true` keeps kdenlive's own settings (`40`/`160`/`70`), which also harden and darken the whole picture.

Default: `{noise: 12}`
